title: Gotrade Daily: Big Banks Kick Off Q3 Earnings
summary: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo open Q3 earnings season tonight as memory-chip stocks stay under pressure. See tonight's Gotrade Daily watchlist.
body_markdown:
### Memory-chip stocks stay under pressure


**Micron** ([MU](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mu/) ) fell 3.88% to close at $989.04 on Monday and slipped another 1.9% after hours. The trigger: CXMT announced progress on a 4F² DRAM architecture and plans to launch DDR5 server memory before the end of 2026. In South Korea, Samsung Electronics fell 7.49% and SK Hynix fell 8.60% ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-micron-technology-stock-sliding-today-93CH-4945275) ).


## Pre-Market Pulse 📊


As of 11:12pm ET Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.8% at 30,646.50 and S&P 500 futures were down 0.2% at 7,840. Dow futures were up 0.2% at 52,187, in line with money moving out of tech and into more defensive sectors ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stock-futures-steady-as-bank-earnings-inflation-data-loom-4945262) ).


## Macro Note 📝


Brent crude settled at $105.46 and WTI at $92.57 a barrel on Monday after strikes on Riyadh's airport ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stock-futures-muted-as-oil-stays-above-100-ahead-of-earnings-4943768) ). September CPI is due Wednesday, followed by PPI and retail sales on Thursday.


## Conclusion


Tonight, the bank reports are the first test of Q3 earnings season. They could give an early read on US credit and consumer conditions ahead of Wednesday's inflation data.


Meanwhile, the pressure on memory-chip stocks shows the market remains sensitive to competitive news.
